Messages.Author: Astardel
Messages.Body:
The card text says:
----
Requires a ready vampire. If this vampire is Ravnos, this action is at +1
stealth. Put this card on the acting vampire. During your untap phase, burn
this card, and each other Methuselah chooses a ready vampire he or she
controls who is not older than this vampire. If you control a ready
Lasombra, you choose the vampires instead. This vampire and the chosen
vampires go to torpor.
----

Well, while playing has come out a question on the meaning of "you choose
the vampires instead". Does the Lasombra playing the Purge still have to
choose not-older vampires, or could (i.e.) Igniatio send into torpor old
aunt Arika?

Sorry for the maybe stupid question but we (I and my playing group) have not
still totally mastered the English grammar -__-

Messages.Author: Ira
Messages.Body:
If you don't control a ready Lasombra when the Purge is played, but
you do control a ready Lasombra when the Purge is burned, do you get
to pick the vampires? Is there precedent for this sort of thing, and
if so, what should I be using to guide myself to the correct answer?
I couldn't think of anything similar.

Ira

Messages.Author: Daneel
Messages.Body:



Baltimore Purge [CE:U]
Cardtype: Action

Requires a ready vampire.
If this vampire is Ravnos, this action is at +1 stealth. Put this card
on the acting vampire. During your untap phase, burn this card, and each
other Methuselah chooses a ready vampire he or she controls who is not
older than this vampire. If you control a ready Lasombra, you choose the
vampires instead. This vampire and the chosen vampires go to torpor.

I think that the key to assessing this is the timing of the effects of
the card. The first part - basically, the first two sentences - are
relevant when playing the card, and the rest is basically ignored until
the trigger event ("during your untap phase") occurs. It is then that
the rest of the effect is assessed and resolved. Part of that delayed
effect checks whether you have a ready Lasombra in play.

--
Bye,

Daneel
